decision: Do not continue a local ProxyBridge repair as the complete Windows containment backend under the current requirements.
scope: Bounded supported-interface review and an isolated diagnostic draft; not an executed patched Windows prototype.
user_stop_condition: Stop rather than repeating many hours of exploratory implementation when no bounded repair path satisfies selected-instance containment and failure blocking.

mandatory_gates.name: Transparent TCP and UDP
mandatory_gates.finding: The prior HTTP/SOCKS probes explicitly connect to the bypassed local Mihomo port. Transparent application TCP remains unproven. Local UDP bypass was observed previously, but its exact cause remains unproven.

mandatory_gates.name: Instance and descendant attribution
mandatory_gates.finding: NETWORK supports packet modification but has no PID metadata. FLOW supplies PID but cannot block. SOCKET supplies PID and can block, but cannot modify or re-inject events. Job membership alone does not install network policy. Image/path-wide denial would affect unselected instances of the same application.

mandatory_gates.name: Engine/service loss and DNS
mandatory_gates.finding: WinDivert uses per-handle dynamic WFP sessions. Cleanup reinjects queued non-sniff packets that have not timed out; destruction uninstalls callouts and closes the WFP engine. The original ProxyBridge disconnect path stops the capture engine. No independently surviving per-instance denial layer or system-DNS caller attribution was established.

rejected_shortcuts: PID or descendant polling alone does not establish enforcement before a new child first sends.
Dropping all unattributed host traffic can affect unselected applications.
A persistent WFP application-path filter does not distinguish selected and unselected instances of the same executable.
A restart watchdog does not establish blocking throughout the failure interval.
Job kill-on-close does not document an atomic ordering that blocks network before all network filter handles are closed.
Keeping a WinDivert handle in another user-mode process merely introduces another lifetime dependency; no general persistent per-instance guarantee is proven.

isolated_diagnostic_draft.capability: Draft adds a true direct-destination TCP probe and per-case UDP lifecycle observations. It does not implement the missing containment layer.

next_step: Stop this repair attempt and discuss a different Windows backend design. Do not start more policy variations or long VM tests without a concrete independent instance-identity and failure-blocking design.

sources.scope: Layer capability matrix: NETWORK has no PID; FLOW observation only; SOCKET has PID/block but no event injection.
Queued packet reinjection on handle cleanup.
Callout uninstall and WFP engine closure.
Client disconnect stops and unloads engine.
Dynamic objects end with session; persistent object lifetime alone does not supply per-instance identity.
User and application path conditions require appropriate scope; no direct general PID condition for these management filters.
Job membership and kill-on-close do not constitute an independently surviving network denial policy.
